response.sql: WITH inv AS (SELECT invoice_number, AVG(CAST(product_quantity AS REAL)) AS avg_quantity, AVG((derived_product_cost - derived_total_cost) / NULLIF(derived_total_cost, 0)) AS cost_ratio FROM Invoice_Line_Items GROUP BY invoice_number), overall AS (SELECT AVG(avg_quantity) AS overall_avg FROM inv) SELECT inv.invoice_number, inv.avg_quantity, inv.cost_ratio, inv.avg_quantity - overall.overall_avg AS quantity_above_average FROM inv CROSS JOIN overall WHERE inv.avg_quantity > overall.overall_avg ORDER BY (quantity_above_average IS NULL), quantity_above_average DESC LIMIT 10;

assumptions.assumption: The query is written for SQLite, the dialect implied by the INTEGER PRIMARY KEY and DATETIME definitions. CAST(... AS REAL) and NULLIF are used accordingly.
product_quantity is VARCHAR but holds plain numeric text, so it is cast to REAL before averaging. Non-numeric text would be coerced by SQLite (for example '3 units' becomes 3) rather than excluded.
A line whose derived_total_cost is 0 or NULL has no defined cost ratio, so its ratio is NULL and is ignored in the per-invoice average. Null quantities are likewise ignored.
The overall average is the unweighted mean of the per-invoice average quantities across all invoices, computed before the above-average filter is applied.
An invoice whose quantity average is NULL is excluded by the filter, so the 'missing last' ordering is a safeguard that does not change the result.
